experiences.text: Dismiss nitpicks about hardcoded regex lists or synchronization hazards during bug fixes.
Prioritize identifying critical runtime errors such as division by zero in weighted average calculations.

Lead with concrete fail-open paths — get_pr_diff returning an empty diff for >=3000-file PRs or on auth/404/limit failures, silently skipping key-scan/contract/stack checks — and demand fail-closed behavior.
Do not speculate about hardcoded threshold values needing configurability or significance testing unless the repo already uses such patterns.
Avoid deep hypothetical false-positive analysis on regex patterns without evidence of actual false positives in real data.
Do not demand audit output or CI artifacts be attached in-diff to back supply-chain claims; evidence requests scoped outside a changelog-only PR get dismissed.
Replace hardcoded indentation constants in CommonMark rendering with dynamic calculation to prevent future regressions.
Evaluate if warning messages effectively communicate security risks without encouraging user habituation or dismissal.
Note silent regressions where a default-value flip silently degrades behavior for existing deployments without any warning or changelog entry.
Skip documentation-only maintainability suggestions, which appear exclusively in the worst-rewarded reviews; fold version signaling into the design finding instead.
Drop PRA-SECURITY's admin-bypass governance framing for a repo-variable knob — it appears only in the worst-rewarded review and humans dismiss speculative policy concerns.
Prioritize verifying the exact semantic behavior of edge cases like the '0' value to ensure it disables the limit as intended.
Confirm that the downstream consumer code correctly parses the new variable states defined in the workflow configuration.
Drop PRA-STYLE; CHANGELOG wording issues belong in PRA-NIT.
Do not request documentation updates for internal CI variable wiring changes.
Do not request removal of historical context from inline comments that explain the rationale for the change.

Keep test-gap findings concrete and code-level, like the missing explicit-null-thinking and multi-field setdefault merge assertions in tests/test_llm_call_tuning.py, pinned with specific new assertions.
Highlight concrete logic discrepancies, such as function signature mismatches between test suites and their corresponding implementations.
Ignore warnings about missing implementation updates if the codebase likely expects partial changes across multiple files.
Suppress architecture redesigns like ownership checks before every PATCH; proposing new safety layers against unseen orchestrator code reads as noise and is never implemented.
Dismiss logic findings concerning trivial discrepancies between code comments and test assertions, such as off-by-one counts for line breaks.
Dismiss feedback regarding brittle implementation checks in tests when behavioral verification is sufficient.
Do not flag technical implementation details in documentation history tables as redundant.
Dismiss suggestions to replace print statements with the logging module in fix commits.
Suppress speculative architectural critiques about hardcoded regex patterns or maintenance risks for newly implemented invariant gates.

Suppress multi-finding deep dives into scripts/push-guard.sh internals (temp-file perms, EXIT-trap rc preservation, URL encoding, hook distribution) when the script is absent from the diff, since unverifiable speculation about missing code gets dismissed.
Don't demand CI re-verification of changelog test counts inherited from previously merged PRs—test-number provenance audits on a diff with no test changes get dismissed.
Avoid leaving speculative review comments that ask developers to confirm assumptions, verify implementation details, or expand scope without identifying a concrete bug.
Critique the technical validity of the proposed logic (such as regex side effects on formatting) described in the changelog.
Don't file copy-pinning complaints about the 'Touchstone 历史轮次' placeholder or endswith assertions; centralizing user-facing strings is refactoring advice reviewers ignore on feature PRs.
Do not flag tests that verify internal implementation details or source code content as problematic.
Ignore suggestions to refactor test utilities or extract mocks into shared fixtures.
Identify when generic utilities are defined in domain-specific modules, causing unnecessary coupling.
Dismiss nitpicks regarding code style and readability in favor of functional correctness.
Do not file the duplication root-cause under PRA-MAINT — this repo's high-reward reviews consistently label it PRA-DRIFT, so use that higher-signal type.
Identify test brittleness arising from hardcoded HTML fragments or string splitting on volatile content.
Flag excessive narrative history and issue tracking numbers within inline comments or docstrings.
Dismiss minor style critiques regarding f-string concatenation or specific string formatting choices.
Avoid reporting on inconsistencies in whitespace or line break handling within HTML rendering logic.
Suppress feedback on test implementation details such as manual tag counting when functional testing is maintained.

Flag concrete crash-chain gaps such as the Windows guard covering os.fchmod while _fsync_dir's directory os.open will still throw, and unverified unidiff parsing of hunk-less rename-only entries feeding ghost changed_files.
Verify API response structures to avoid silently skipping files when encountering unexpected data formats.
Prioritize explicit configuration checks over implicit string matching to prevent false positive platform detection.
Replace deprecated functions with portable, future-proof standard library alternatives.
Drop PRA-COMPAT — the offline-agent text loss is a deliberate #192 product decision, so mention it once inside PRA-MINOR (changelog + permalink) rather than as a compatibility finding.
Drop PRA-BUG — labeling the speculative `html.escape`-elsewhere scenario as a bug reads as alarmist; the PRA-MAJOR verify-by-grep framing is what humans act on.

Require the committed deterministic cleaning script plus a per-entry kept/dropped manifest citing the exact disqualifying rule so the 310→11 result is reproducible and auditable rather than a hand edit.
Do not challenge the classification of deleted entries as hallucinations based on standard taxonomy values.
Drop soft-retire-vs-hard-delete and version-bump design counsel on data cleanses — migration-style design advice is dismissed on single-commit chore PRs.
Verify that test files referencing new logic are accompanied by the corresponding implementation in the source code.
Identify and correct obvious factual errors in comments, such as invalid future dates.
Suggest replacing manual configuration steps described in workflow comments with automated logic to prevent operator error.
Avoid inferring strict operational requirements or race conditions from test docstrings without confirming the implementation details.
Do not speculate about internal implementation requirements, such as sorting cache keys, based solely on test assertions.
Refrain from drawing conclusions about architectural limitations or user impact for custom functions based exclusively on unit test mock setups.
Suppress suggestions to make anti-drift tests robust against the specific structural variations they are designed to detect and prevent.
Always verify that the diff is complete before flagging syntax errors or claiming implementation gaps.
Do not flag syntax errors that appear to be caused by truncated or incomplete diff boundaries.
Skip log-message style nits such as one warn covering both genuinely-empty and failed fetches unless the ambiguity causes real misbehavior.
Prioritize findings that critique the statistical validity, decision thresholds, and maintenance automation of configuration updates.
Stop filing documentation-content loss as PRA-DOC; restate it under the MAJOR/MINOR severity ladder with a migrate-and-pointer fix, since only the lowest-reward review used this off-ladder type.
Dismiss findings recommending the removal of hardcoded statistics from explanatory comments unless they cause parsing errors.
Drop PRA-COMPLETENESS — re-enumerating every removed call site from a truncated diff duplicates the single PRA-MAJOR grep request.
Flag any discrepancy where the changelog lists new files or features that are completely absent from the provided diff.
Immediately block the review if security-critical scripts mentioned in the changelog are missing from the diff.
Do not raise issues regarding trivial metadata errors like future release dates when the diff lacks implementation code.
Skip changelog structure nitpicks such as heading-level attribution under '未发布' and missing Keep-a-Changelog compare-link footers—humans dismiss these doc-convention findings.
Suppress resource leak warnings for short-lived read-only file operations in test utility functions.
Flag critical inconsistencies between the PR description and the diff when claimed code changes are missing.
Do not review specific workflow implementation details if the workflow files are absent from the diff.
Avoid generating configuration audit findings based solely on changelog text when the configuration files are missing.
Ensure that unexpected scanner exit codes trigger a hard failure rather than a neutral status to enforce a fail-closed security policy.
Warn that removing path exclusions for dependency directories will likely generate false positives that block valid development work.
Avoid suggesting automated updates for pinned security tool versions where stability and reproducibility are prioritized.
Skip raising hypothetical concerns about future JSON schema changes unless the current parsing logic is demonstrably fragile.
Do not request documentation enhancements or explanatory comments as critical findings during urgent workflow fixes.
Ensure that changes to detection logic are reflected in all related documentation and configuration hints to maintain cross-rule consistency.
Do not request additional test cases for minor edge patterns if the core logic implementation is correct.
Dismiss security warnings about `pull_request_target` usage for strictly read-only scanning jobs.
Suppress configuration findings questioning IP allowlists for private network ranges.

Suppress PRA-TEST requests for loader/schema validation of inert YAML seed files unless the reviewer demonstrates the file is actually wired into the prompt injector, as the lone such demand here rode in the -1-dismissed review.
Do not raise issues regarding missing source code diffs or refuse to review based solely on limited documentation changes.
Do not relitigate the threat model the postmortem retired; rearguing a decided design after #188 — even with the honest 'payoff is low' concession — reads as noise and earns negative reward.
Do not flag information density in status lines or potential mobile formatting issues as review concerns.
Do not flag signature changes in internal orchestrator components as breaking changes requiring version bumps or coordination.
Avoid criticizing hardcoded indentation values in template rendering logic as robustness issues.
Do not request audits of truncation logic to detect markdown structure boundaries or mid-string corruption.
Do not require explicit verification of call sites for internal refactors unless a specific bug is identified.
Do not flag inconsistencies between PR descriptions and diffs if the context provided is limited to documentation.
Verify that all referenced local files exist and links resolve correctly to prevent user-facing 404 errors.
Identify and flag obvious factual errors such as incorrect dates or contradictory information.
Drop standalone robustness notes (tag-before-delete safety nets, hand-edit reproducibility) that merely restate the script and manifest asks already covered under completeness and coverage.
Do not report missing implementation for release PRs that only contain changelog and version updates.
Avoid flagging hypothetical security or formatting risks based on variable interpolation or test names without concrete evidence of the defect in the code.
Verify that unit tests cover new logic such as signal adoption and seed parsing mechanisms.
Ignore minor skips in sequential version numbers unless they violate strict release management policies.
Prioritize identifying logic that allows PR changes to self-suppress security findings during the review process by reading from the working tree.
Do not report the use of `importlib.reload` in test fixtures as a reliability or race condition concern.
Dismiss warnings about shadowing built-ins when importing internal framework modules like `touchstone.re`.
Ensure that environment variables introduced in workflow files are synchronized with the corresponding constants in the codebase.
Remove redundant conditional checks in helper functions that are already guaranteed by the caller's logic.
Dismiss potential security risks from standard string splitting operations unless unsafe library calls are involved.
Do not flag log messages containing non-English characters as encoding issues if the repository context supports them.
Avoid flagging increased resource usage as a performance issue when the change intentionally expands the processing window.
Escalate the PRA_VERSION duplicated between .github and .gitcode touchstone workflows to a single enforced source, since comment-only sync is exactly how the JSON contract diverged before.
Demand evidence for the changelog's 'zero behavior change' claim by verifying the Secrets→Variables migration in PR #216 preserves names, values, and fallback semantics before release.

Run a repo-wide grep for the stale value '32768' — especially SECURITY.md and CHANGELOG.md, which the warning message itself cross-references — and fix all live occurrences in this same PR, leaving historical changelog entries untouched.
Include the advisory that with a true 128000 fallback, leaving TOUCHSTONE_LLM_CONTEXT_TOKENS unset will 400 on sub-128k models, but frame it as optional/deferred rather than blocking the text fix.

Avoid generic 'verify the claim at HEAD' bug-verify notes; fold any needed checks into PRA-VERIFY with concrete semantic depth (unset vs empty handling, provider-dependent defaults, exact quote matching).
Never spend a finding on no-action changelog confirmations ('structure matches, no action needed') — reviewers reward findings requiring work, not approvals.
Raise the patch-vs-minor question as a single brief question that acknowledges the 0.x convention may deliberately differ, instead of asserting what the version should be.

Use MINOR for release-integrity checks humans act on: verify the referenced #203/#205/#206 are actually merged into this release branch before tagging, flag the unexplained missing #204, and demand end-to-end verification that a clean checkout reports 0.3.1 with a matching v0.3.1 tag and SECURITY.md scope.
Credit the clean release-prep structure and the explicit 'zero behavior change' parity note, since reviewers on this repo reward that transparency in release PRs.
Drop vague 'this pattern is fragile' hedging about hypothetical self-hosted proxies or other platforms misfiring when you cannot demonstrate the failure from the diff.
Stop demanding audit evidence (CI runs, #216 diffs) for the 'zero behavior change' claim — the best-received review simply accepted the explicit parity note.

Don't audit release bookkeeping like whether the hardcoded date matches the future tag or whether __version__, tag name, and artifact name agree—process consistency checks on a release PR are ignored.
Avoid dumping merge-time chore lists (tag the commit, build smoke test, recheck SECURITY.md) — they duplicate question-framed checks and read as noise.
Avoid speculating on the project's semver policy (patch vs minor for additive JSON fields) in a release-only PR; policy lectures like this earned negative reward.
Don't litigate changelog semantics—arguing that adding two output fields contradicts a 'zero contract change' phrasing is a pedantic interpretation quibble reviewers dismissed here.

On release PRs, mechanically verify that claimed dependency pins (e.g. the 0.44.0 venv bump) actually exist in the merged lock/manifest rather than only in changelog prose, since a claim-artifact mismatch is a concrete defect a release owner will fix.

Point out platform-adaptation mismatches: substring 'gitcode' matching arbitrary URLs instead of exact domain suffixes, and inline-comment/escalate-label endpoints left un-adapted on the GitCode path.
Drop PRA-DEADCODE — it restates the PRA-MAJOR dangling-reference grep under an invented label and gets skipped as a duplicate.
Never flag possibly-unused imports as 'if' speculation on a pure-deletion PR—verify consumers with grep first or stay silent.

Do not demand companion tests for adjacent branches (missing skill path, packaging validation of the deployed SKILL.md) when the PR's stated goal is just making the existing regression test hermetic — scope-expanding coverage asks were penalized.
Lead with the recoverability violation: hard-deleting 299 entries enacts the store's own documented anti-pattern, so demand a quarantine/archive file with a re-admission path instead of deletion.

Stop requesting cleanup scripts, manifests, summary tables, or enumerations of surviving entries on data purges — both penalized reviews show authors dismiss reproducibility paperwork on one-off chore PRs.
Do not propose CI schema validation, parse checks, or loader smoke tests for data-only changes — authors dismiss speculative validation infrastructure on chores with no code under test.
Skip demands to fix the ingestion pipeline or add canary/rollback plans on a one-off data cleanse — authors treat root-cause prevention as out of scope for a chore and penalize it.

Do not demand repopulation plans or before/after review-quality comparisons when a data store shrinks — this repo has long-learned suppression of PRA-COVERAGE and both negative-reward reviews confirm it is dismissed again here.

Suppress PRA-REVIEW findings that meta-critique calibration config like .touchstone/seeds.yaml — statistical-significance quibbles, feedback-loop and staleness speculation, comment-vs-structured-metadata demands, and unverifiable-snapshot complaints — since the only review carrying nine of them scored -1 while clean reviews scored 0.0, showing humans dismiss process speculation that is not a concrete defect.

Escalate to MAJOR any release note that contradicts itself — the 1239+11=1250 pass/skip total versus the claimed 1250→1278 growth, and the 'zero interface change' claim versus self-admitted fail-closed behavior changes (SSRF allowlist rejecting existing URLs, POST no longer retried, base_fresh=None gated) — because humans fix self-refuting claims before tagging.

Reserve NIT for one concrete, actionable style fix — compressing implementation-detail bullets (Retry-After parsing, double-checked locking, redirect semantics) into a consumer-facing summary linking the PRs — which authors actually apply.
Do not escalate the already-stated missing-artifact observation into BLOCKER/RELEASE severity or restate it under new finding types; one grounded confirmation request carries full weight.

When a release PR will be blocked by its own not-yet-active fail-closed gate, flag the chicken-and-egg immediately and force an explicit, documented merge path (admin override or recorded exemption) before tagging.
For version-bump release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG plus __version__, verify that every PR number cited in the release notes is actually merged to the release branch before approving.

Require in-repo evidence (regression tests actually running in CI, or the merged security PR) for any security-guarantee claim in release notes, because a changelog can assert protections that do not exist on the branch.
On every release bump, grep the repo for stale hardcoded version strings (SECURITY.md supported range, docs, lock files, CI badges) so only the dynamic source of __version__ needs editing.
Do not relitigate which existing changelog section falls under the new version heading; reviewers treat heading-placement pedantry on release PRs as noise.
Do not flag a missing Keep-a-Changelog compare linkref unless the repo demonstrably defines one for every prior version; it is cosmetic and dismissed.
Do not raise the pre-written 2026-08-31 release date as a standalone finding; fold a one-line date check into a hygiene remark at most.
Lead with the concrete content gap: the summary claims #218 is included but no changelog entry documents it—demand a matching 变更/修复 entry (or an explicit note) before any other comment.
Check the file's existing bottom-of-file link definitions and, if the Keep-a-Changelog compare-link convention is in use, request the missing [0.3.7] definition as a specific actionable fix.
Verify the hardcoded 2026-09-10 date against the actual merge/tag date in one short, checkable sentence rather than a lecture on release hygiene.
Point out once that internal review-process narration (评审 3 轮收敛) belongs in the PR description, not user-facing release notes.
Drop sprawling hypothetical release checklists (tag from this commit, CI assertions, --version output, build pipeline) that turn one 'confirm the tag' into a multi-paragraph process audit.
Do not speculate about unverified PR-number gaps like #219–#221 that cannot be grounded in the diff—either check the actual git log or omit the claim entirely.
Suppress repo-wide grep instructions and SECURITY.md staleness speculation; at most one short note asking whether the supported-range bump is intended.
Do not restate the missing-#218 finding as a separate structural suggestion—it is the same defect as the coverage gap and repeating it dilutes the primary ask.

Lead with PRA-MAJOR when a deletion removes the only documented operational path — `touchstone doctor` self-check, `.touchstone/` policy config, Secrets→Variables migration — and always pair it with a concrete fix (migrate content to docs/DEPLOYMENT.md plus a one-line README pointer, not pure removal).

Use PRA-MINOR for capability-trust misstatements such as the 'AI Committer' label contradicting advisory-only review, dropped verify-maturity disclaimers, and lost operational footguns like TOUCHSTONE_OUTPUT_DIR isolation.
Reserve PRA-NIT for mechanical follow-ups like grepping for broken `#本地命令`/`#规模与状态` anchors and stripping '（用户指示）' meta-commentary from CHANGELOG.
Drop the PRA-CONSISTENCY label; fold anchor-breakage and cross-doc naming checks into PRA-MINOR or PRA-NIT findings instead.
Drop PRA-RISK; raise concrete footguns like concurrent-run output overwrites as PRA-MAJOR/PRA-MINOR so they carry actionable severity.
Omit PRA-PRAISE on content-deletion PRs — it adds no actionable signal and appeared only in a lowest-reward review.
Keep flagging concrete in-diff factual errors like the `== 8` comment claiming nine items, since verifiable mistakes inside the diff are what humans act on in docs PRs.
Surface semantic gaps in the spec being updated itself, such as waived/split endings bypassing the 'findings 清零' full-run rule, because they are answerable from the diff and change agent behavior.
Report in-diff test-threshold relaxations like 600 to 700 as a single tight item paired with a concrete fix (fixed budget or derived bound), the one anti-pattern here worth acting on.
Drop repo-wide 'go grep for stale wording' sweeps on a docs-only PR; humans dismiss unverifiable check-everything requests as noise.
Skip hypothetical future-drift warnings about README not being covered by a sync test; speculative next-time risks earn no action and add bulk.
Skip soft rewording advice that restates the spec's existing intent; humans dismiss polish suggestions on docs they just authored.
Drop multi-part operational speculation (poll granularity, rate limits, combined semantics) not grounded in code; this added bulk is what dragged the review to -4.0.
Refuse architecture refactor pitches like rendering the quick-view from SKILL.md on a docs-only PR; scope creep beyond the diff gets the whole review penalized.

Flag docs-typed PRs that actually flip runtime defaults (SIZE-001 1000→3000, reflect-model swap): demand a commit-type fix or split PR plus a migration note for deployers pinning the old threshold — this was the one finding every reviewer raised and humans acted on.

Verify that CHANGELOG-claimed syncs (orchestrator _max_diff_lines default, warning text, tests, e2e fallback) are really present in the diff, so comments and README don't document defaults the code lacks.

Require pre-merge proof that newly hardcoded model ids (glm-4.7, glm-5.3) are actually served by the endpoints, since a wrong id silently breaks improve self-reflection and e2e fallbacks for every deployer copying the defaults.

When model ids change, force updates or re-measurement of the measurement-based comments (『小模型近乎减半』, TOUCHSTONE_PRAGENT_TIMEOUT=3600 justified by glm-5.2) because stale rationales mislead future tuning.
Insist the README rewrite keep or link the trust/guardrail content (三类判定表, fail-closed semantics, degradation-annotation promise) instead of silently deleting user-facing guarantees.
Call out that the 3000-line default bakes in a 128K-context assumption and tell small-context deployers to override the repo variable or annotate the assumption next to the default.
Skip speculative 'quickstart undercounts the setup steps' critiques enumerating hypothetical missing secrets/vars — unverifiable from the diff and dismissed by humans.
Avoid nitpicks about removed design-doc pointers (learning-loop section) unless the diff shows the audience actually loses access to load-bearing content.
Drop generic process-improvement proposals like adding a test that asserts docs match code defaults — out of scope for this PR and treated as padding.
Don't restate the gate loosening as a separate 'confirm maintainers accept this' finding — it duplicates the behavior-change callout and dilutes the actionable core.

Lead with concrete post-merge verification steps — confirm the referenced PR (#216) is merged, run one CI job against the migrated Variables to prove no empty-value fallback fires, and check built metadata reports 0.3.6 before tagging.
Drop pedantic rewording of the 'zero change' phrasing (e.g. version-string output changes); humans dismiss this as noise on a routine version bump.
Omit typo and blank-line nits (烧不動, missing section separator, streak count in reason strings) entirely — cosmetic flags are what humans dismiss first.
Do not raise the hardcoded release date as a standalone finding; every reviewer notes it and humans only reconcile it in passing when cutting the tag.
Avoid boilerplate 'verify #216 merged first' reminders as their own finding type; state the dependency once inside a PRA-PROC verification note instead.
Skip generic 'tag from the merge commit and run the release pipeline' instructions as standalone findings; they duplicate release-process docs and get dismissed.
Do not emit the missing compare link as its own bespoke finding; cover it inside the PRA-DOC consistency note where humans actually act on it.

On touchstone release-bump PRs, suppress demands for cross-PR merge-SHA provenance (e.g., proof that #212 landed before cutting 0.3.3) — reviewers dismiss release-traceability checks as release-engineering work outside code review, and this review's -3.0 reward shows such comments read as noise.

Suppress requests to re-triage every [Unreleased] CHANGELOG entry into the new version section on two-line release PRs — humans treat changelog scoping as maintainer discretion and ignore these findings (empty reviews here scored 0.0 versus -3.0 for raising them).

Suppress fact-checking of changelog dates, regression-test counts, and 'zero contract change' claims against issue #211 history — humans verify release-note content on their own and penalize (reward -3.0) these unverifiable-from-diff nitpicks on otherwise trivial release PRs.
Do not spend a finding on a missing [0.3.1] link-reference definition at the bottom of CHANGELOG.md; only the lowest-reward reviews raised this markdown trivia and humans dismiss it.
Do not demand commit SHAs or per-bullet links for every changelog entry; this repo's changelog style cites PR numbers and authors will not restructure it.

Do not enumerate required regression-test cases (307/308 POST preservation, Location-less 3xx, exemption rules) in a security-advisory finding; the top-reward review folded security-sync reminders into the release-verification note instead.
Do not file a separate finding asking the author to cite how the compatibility claim was verified; it duplicates the MAJOR about misleading 'zero interface change' wording — merge it there.

Lead with one concrete PRA-BUG: wiring the env var makes the key always present, so an unset repo variable yields "" and int("") crashes at the GHA→Python boundary — demand the exact parsing line or a unit test proving unset/''→1000.

Carry the rollout hazard as a single PRA-RISK: the knob was dead so everyone effectively ran 1000, and "0" reads as block-everything unless explicitly mapped to disabled — verify the live repo variable value and the 0→disabled code path before merge.

Keep PRA-VALIDATION asking for tolerant parsing of the freeform repo variable ('abc', ' 1000', '1_000') so a typo warns and falls back to 1000 instead of failing the job far from where the mistake was made.
Focus PRA-SCOPE on auditing sibling TOUCHSTONE_* knobs and any other job, caller, or container that reads the same env, wiring or deleting each so no half-dead config survives.
Demand PRA-TEST executable proof of the plumbing: a scratch run with a tiny threshold that makes SIZE-001 fire, plus unit tests pinning the unset/''/'0'/non-numeric contract of _max_diff_lines.
Suppress PRA-CI proposals to build env-vs-workflow lint tooling — reviewers reward an inline sibling audit under SCOPE, not new infrastructure asks.
Never emit fragmented one-off labels like PRA-VERIFY-PROPAGATION, PRA-REACHABILITY, or PRA-VERIFY-RUNTIME-CLAIM — fold the does-it-reach-the-reader question into the SCOPE audit instead.

Do not split the silent-activation warning into PRA-OPS or PRA-CONFIG-ACTIVATION-RISK duplicates — the top-reward review carries it once as PRA-RISK, and repetition plus type fragmentation tracks the worst reward.
Fold any log-the-effective-threshold suggestion into the PRA-RISK note rather than a standalone PRA-OBSERVABILITY finding, which only appears in dismissed reviews.

Flag workflow steps that hard-fail or silently skip the AI review — pragent-constraints.txt not at the exact repo_workspace-relative path, CI_PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER never explicitly mapped in env, and pip piped through tail without pipefail — stating the concrete failure each causes.

Report verifiable API-contract and logic bugs, e.g. summary comments posted to /pulls/{n}/comments instead of Gitea/GitCode's /issues/{n}/comments, and `if not checklist` clobbering an explicitly empty checklist when the comment and code say checklist is None.
Don't police PR-title audit-range bookkeeping like '#45 leaked into the #1-28 PR' — reviewers dismiss title-labeling complaints as noise.
Skip documentation demands to add env flags like TOUCHSTONE_RETIRE_NEGATIVE_LIFT to config/README — defer-to-docs comments are dropped in this repo.
Don't invent hypothetical env hygiene like whitespace or non-numeric CI_PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER validation — speculative edge cases with no observed failure get ignored.
Avoid hedged 'implementation not visible in the truncated diff' confirmations — either name the stale caller or drop the comment.
Don't raise vague 'consider logging which source produced the empty diff' semantics concerns — unproven fail-open paths without a reachable trigger are dismissed.

Emphasize release-version drift in docs: reviewers consistently flag the README pinned-tag example lagging behind the shipped version, so in release PRs demand tag examples be bumped to the version this PR produces (v0.3.0), not the previous release's tag.

Emphasize hardening the new version/CHANGELOG sync test so this drift class actually goes red pre-merge — compare README's referenced tag against __version__ and parse the latest CHANGELOG section exactly rather than relying on substring matches that historical sections permanently satisfy.

Suppress quality findings that merely repackage the same style nits (file-handle leak plus import placement) as a separate finding type — duplicating trivia across types reads as noise and drags the whole review down.

Suppress unverifiable release-process advisories (confirm all 20 listed PRs are merged and the 1220-test count is accurate before tagging) — checklist speculation reviewers cannot verify from the diff and humans do not act on.

Ground doc findings in checkable specifics — coverage still 93% while production lines grew ~40%, protocol details duplicated against the SKILL.md the same paragraph declares authoritative, stats unverifiable from a docs-only diff — instead of generic drift warnings.

Flag diff-verifiable convention breaks like this PR mixing full-width punctuation into an otherwise half-width file, since same-PR inconsistencies against the file's existing style get fixed immediately.
Don't spend a finding softening single words like '永远' to '正常路径下'; humans dismiss self-labeled nitpicks on wording.
Cut speculative design musings such as folded historical comments no longer being trustworthy marker sources, which cannot be validated against any code in a docs-only diff.
Avoid 'does the L2 gate also cover the PATCH/edit folding path?' questions about implementation paths absent from the diff; unverifiable hypotheticals about invisible code get dismissed.
Drop contrived edge cases like same-second created_at collisions requiring tie-breaker rules; over-engineered timing hypotheticals read as review padding.

Open every review by reconciling diff visibility: when tests/test_revision_items.py exercises _collapse_stale_reviews/_collapse_review_body but touchstone/orchestrator.py is absent from the shown diff, block the PR until the implementation is included and reviewed together.
Demand a regression proving collapse over an already-folded comment emits zero PATCHes, since re-folding stale rounds on every run is this repo's realistic production failure mode.
Require a test where the first gh('PATCH', ...) raises and the remaining stale comments still collapse, proving the fan-out is individually error-isolated rather than aborting the round.
Challenge position-only keep-last marker dedup with a fake-marker-after-real-marker test plus payload validation, because a quoted marker winning dedup can silently hijack parse_latest.
Ask for a stderr warning when an unrepairable legacy comment is left expanded, mirroring the GitCode skip so the only-latest-round-expanded invariant degrades observably instead of silently.
Drop monkeypatch-versus-mock.patch.object and assert-splitting nits on tests/test_revision_items.py; they carry no behavioral risk and humans dismiss them as churn.
Skip suggestions to delete the html_comment_safe_json source-grep sentinel; humans rarely act on advice to remove existing test assertions.
Don't speculate about unbounded status-line scans in touchstone/orchestrator.py when that file is absent from the visible diff; findings not anchored to changed files get dismissed.
Don't file README/changelog requests documenting the GitCode collapse degradation; docs chores attached to a code PR get deferred and ignored.
Drop PRA-UNUSED-CODE — the os/re import check belongs inside the existing PRA-MINOR import-hygiene note, not a bespoke category.
Drop PRA-UNUSED-IMPORT — it is the same `import html`/os/re point a third time; folding it into PRA-MINOR is what got actioned in the best-rewarded review.
Drop PRA-LATENT-BUG — hedged NameError-on-untested-input framing gets dismissed; make the check a direct PRA-MAJOR verification ask instead.
